text:
Mason McTavish's first season in St. Louis started well and then went quiet. The third pick of 2021, traded from Anaheim after 304 games, has seven goals and 12 points in 21 games, but only two points in his last 10 and none in five straight. This week the story was the Ducks coming to town; the Blues won Tuesday, though McTavish didn't get on the scoresheet.

Our read is mixed. His own chances are strong for the season, 1.47 expected goals per 60, well up from 1.22 last year, and the Blues have scored 5.5 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which usually swings back. But the recent drought comes with fewer chances too, so it isn't all bounces. Evolving-Hockey's numbers from last season explain the bind: his team created a lot more with him on the ice (86th percentile among forwards) and gave up even more (bottom 2%). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man, 7.9 primary shot assists per 60. Our season projection has him finishing around 49 points.
